cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I'll tune your violin for the audition. I work by ear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. That string couldn't hold pitch. I've saved you a failure onstage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The audition panel heard it snap. They're asking if you know what you're doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I rejected an unreliable string. Ask for their spare violin; I'll check that one before I approve it.

mechanism: A claims that the pupil recognition of a tuning failure proves its musical training while presenting the break as expert quality control.
confusable: Unlike merely taking credit for a pupil, A must sustain a technical bluff against a real public challenge.
comparison: Remote repair expert involvement versus an audition panel hearing the failure directly.
seedUse: Keep D18 snapped string/panel/spare instrument escalation; S05 redirects B correct alarm into a lesson about what to call the event.
